utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First, I would like to put on the record that Mr. Mladic is not present in court. He waived his right yesterday to be absent for the remainder of yesterday's session and for today's session. Mr. Weber, the Chamber was informed that you wanted to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If it's acceptable to the Court I did speak with Mr. Lukic about this also. I was wondering if we could please provide to the witness during today's testimony copies of his report. I have prepared clean copies. He did not have them with him yesterday. The two documents that I prepared to provide to the witness are Exhibit P2605, marked for identification, the report in this case; and 65 ter 10221, which was the Karadzic report that was being prepared -- or that was being discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted. Mr. Lukic, I do understand that you have no problems with it. Then could the witness be -- yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The only thing that the Prosecution would request is that during today's proceedings there are many references to a group or collection of documents and also previous transcript. As much as possible and to assist our ability to actually follow the proceedings, it would be appreciated if we could use precise transcript references to previous testimony or specific documents so that I could follow along with what is going on. It would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the request is clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We got the chart from the Prosecution this morning, so we do not object to this procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I, meanwhile, use the opportunity to ask your attention for the following: Mr. Weber, in its Rule 92 ter motion for Witness Higgs dated the 14th of August, the Prosecution tendered five associated exhibits, namely, Rule 65 ter 18013, 11190, and 14296 up to and including 14298. Now, only number 11190 was tendered and admitted yesterday. Can the Prosecution confirm that the remaining four documents are withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're correct in the fact that I only tendered one. I did review the similarity of material in the document and made the decision based on that. We are not tendering them at this time. However, we are not officially withdrawing them from our exhibit list. I would also note since we're discussing some housekeeping matters that the Prosecution has prepared a final version of that Milosevic testimony transcript. There's a corrected -- non-corrected version used yesterday, and it's available under 30277A. This was Exhibit P2606, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, withdrawal, in the understanding of the Chamber, meant withdrawal from tendering them now, not to remove them from the 65 ter list. Good morning, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to pop up. If there's any way we can please provide the documents discussed before the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may. Could the usher assist. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, I forgot yesterday to ask for the admission of the report from Karadzic case, it's 65 ter 10221, and I spoke with Mr. Weber. If we do not do that, they would be tendering the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct we would be asking for the admission of the full report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since the Defence is now first, it will be assigned a D number. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10221 receives number D395, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D395 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, also, in connection with that, this enlarged map we provided yesterday under number 1D1379. It's just the same map used in this report just admitted, only blown up, so that actual area is more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1379 receives number D396, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The number on the record is not absolutely correct. It should be D396.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's that -- under that number that 1D1379 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D1380 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was provided from the Google Earth, and the bearing of the curb in front of Markale has been determined. Would you agree, Mr. Higgs, with this estimate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As per my re-submitted report it is nearer to 255 or 260 degrees, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We ask for this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We would object based on the limited questions asked so far. I know the -- I think the witness has a stand, and it's a demonstrative exhibit, but I don't have foundation as to how this was calculated precisely and by whom it was calculated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Calculated. It's just ... no, is there any dispute about where north is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- this is taken from Google Earth. If it was created by someone else, I would like the opportunity to the ask that other person about how this was calculated and in what manner. That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, are you serious that we need someone to be called just to identify where north is? Because that seems to be the only thing that counts. All the rest is 165. You take care, what do you call it? A -- geo -- I mean, it's ... fifth grade primary school. That's what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in terms of the calculation of north and the depiction of north on maps or Google Earth, no, that's not my issue. My issue is that there's determinations of angles and other things based on that, that is not as simple as one would purport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing that is added to north is 165 degrees. I'll show you after the break how to do that. And we don't need the witness for that. And the document is admitted. But I'll show you after the break how to do it, Mr. Weber. The number has not been assigned.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1380 receives number D397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, would you agree that this bearing was determined by the 4th French Battalion who was at the scene and that they reached a very approximate value to this one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just confirm which bearing. Do you mean the bearing of the crater?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] The direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. By the French examination team on the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the -- is it the 165 degrees or the 255, Mr. Lukic? Because that's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They said 2800, if -- if we remember -- if I remember correctly. And -- I have it further in the questions so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, just, we have two bearings, two angles on the sheet. Is it the one or is it the other? That's the simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps could the witness answer what the French examination team determined.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the French examination team examined the crater, and from their examination they got the 170 degrees. That is not the same as on this picture here where they've given this 165 to north, because that is an incorrect number. Because between 255 degrees and north, it is not 165. It's actually only 105, so on this picture here north is actually displayed in totally the wrong place. But going back to the original question, it was -- the French did the crater examination where they came up to 170 degrees, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see P797.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say, I'm totally lost with the following sentence you spoke, Witness. You said: "... they got the 170 degrees. That is not the same as on the picture here where they've given this 165 to north ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I do understand that 170 and 165 is not the same. But then you said: "... that is an incorrect number. Because between 255 degrees and north, it's not 165."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. We have 360 degrees in a circle, so it should be 105 degrees, not 165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the difference between the 165 and the 255 is not indicated as -- by number. So, therefore, to say it should be 105 where nothing appears there is surprising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, you're talking about the angle between the red line that goes, if I could say so, more or less south of south-west, or south-west approximately, and the red line that goes down, although a little bit, if I could say so, an easterly direction. Nothing is indicated there what that angle is. So I have difficulties in understanding your explanation why it is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps I pointed at the wrong red lines, but what we see on this picture is an angle, 165 degrees from north. Is that more or less correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road bearing given, which is 255, is actually only 105 degrees from north rather than 165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I am afraid that either I totally misunderstand the picture or you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I think I do. I think -- no, I do understand the picture. I think the witness does not understand the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is my preliminary feeling as well. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand what the witness is saying. I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible to mark this map? Then we could ask the witness to mark the angle which he indicates has 105 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps this one is admitted but we'll now ask the witness to mark what he just wanted to tell us. Could the usher assist. Could you please explain by marking what you meant. And we can always rub it out if there's any need to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Relating to the 165 on this picture, so if the road as we've talked about is on a line of 255 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which road? That road, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is on the angle of 255. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's indicated as 165.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that the first more than half a circle depicts the angle between north and the line that goes to the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. So just to clarify, we're saying that the -- the road which is on 255 is that road, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I now understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I don't think, as a matter of fact, there's a common understanding of everyone about what is depicted and we don't need the marked version of it. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we now have P797 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have seen this report, haven't you? This document, I mean.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 7 in the English. Let's rotate it by 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said today that the French found 170 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at this sketch and tell us what this report says about the findings by the French.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These give a direction of 2850 mills.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which equate to approximately 160 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree that a minute ago you made an error when you said that they came up with 170 degrees?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I'm basing my replies on the evidence I was given, where it is wrote as 170 in some reports, and here, in this one here, you can see it is 160.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, what was read on the spot, which is 2800 equals 175.5 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got the calculation in front of me, but I believe that, yeah, 2850 is nearer 170 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it's not 170. It's 160, as the sketch shows.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see on this sketch here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you find the information that the French finding was 170 degrees? Can you tell us the source?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documentation listed in my report. there is the video, the local Bosnian investigation, as well, and with all those other reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the French. Where did you find specifically that the French finding was 170 degrees?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, my belief -- I can't remember now, but from the -- all those different pieces of evidence, and, again, here, on the mills measurements, so I would have taken it from all of those different sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are dealing with various sources. Again, are you going to give me an answer or not? Where did you find the fact that the French came up with 170 degrees? Because this was part of your today's evidence.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. I can only answer that it was from the evidence I was given here, as you've rightly said, if I had taken it from the mills measurement that is nearer to the 170 to 160, so taken it from all those pieces of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you are challenging the fact that the mills of 1800 [as interpreted] equals 160 degrees; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you say 1800 or 2800.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I misspoke. [Interpretation] 2800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to be very precise it should be 2850. You say that is not 160 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's nearer 170, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, the Chamber would like to see the -- how many mills are there in 360, Mr. Higgs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 6400, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6400. We'll check it. As far as I am aware of, it's 160, 3125, which is closer to 160 than it is to 170. Would you please check that? Could you make the calculation during the break. It's quite simple. 2850 divided by 6400, and then that set out on a scale of 360 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that calculation for Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your new report, you moved the curb bearing by 15 degrees. This has resulted in a changed -- in the direction from which the shell came by only 5 degrees. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- changed the direction of the -- the road to an accurate direction, so nearer to 260 degrees. I then looked at the right angle to that, which is approximately 170, and then looked at the position of the crater and then made that point that the crater is still closely aligned to that direction. I have not done an accurate crater analysis to find out the exact direction as I was just trying to determine whether it is facing in the general direction of 170 or whether it is facing towards the 220/240 which was also mentioned in other reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you then find that there is no inclination to the left. Previously your calculation was 100 degrees. Now it is 90 degrees. This is what we discussed yesterday. Did you change anything in your overall findings? Is there still an inclination to the left or not? And what was the basis, why did you make the change that you did?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is still a slight inclination to the left of the square. So that is still evident. But the general direction of the crater does still face towards the -- closer to the direction of 170 rather than 220.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you demonstrate that in your new sketch in the new report? Did you change anything in your sketch with respect to what you did in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I changed the angle on the -- on the road, the bearing of the road, to make that correct. I then showed a different right angle, which is now 170. So I changed that as well, to give now a far more realistic picture of the bearings in relation to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether my question got lost in translation. I asked you about the conclusion, whether that was changed; and then I asked you about the sketch, whether your conclusion, your new conclusion, was reflected in your sketch. Did you change your sketch to match your new conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion didn't change. My conclusion is still that the round has come from a direction closely around 170 degrees. So that has not changed. I then just altered -- updated the bearings along the road and the right angles so then it does bear true resemblance to the picture of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the picture we're discussing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have -- I think I have one -- 1D document where we can compare both pictures from the previous and from the new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would assist. Because we have on our screens still --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D1391, please. If we can turn it by 90 degrees counter-clockwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Higgs, on the right-hand side you can see a photo that you used in the Karadzic case. On the left-hand side is a photo from the Mladic case. We drew the lines. We moved the photo a bit further off -- up. And we have found that nothing, nothing has been changed in these photos. Are the lines are parallel, just like before in the old photo. And this is what I have asked you: Did you change anything in the way you plotted or made sketches of the situation, or did you just made alterations to your overall conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Can you see that, obviously the line of the curb is still the same. The right angle bearing that I have taken through on the left-hand picture, D1, is 170 degrees. But can you see from the left-hand picture the blue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. You say on the left-hand picture it is 170 degrees. Is it indicated on that picture or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the original picture, yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is the original one? Is that the left one or the right one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my picture on my report for this case, which is the left-hand picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I do have the -- the bearings are all part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- I do not see them at this moment. But perhaps I should have a look at the ... I should look at the report, perhaps. Because nothing is indicated on what we see on our screen at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's only picture. It's page 14 in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please. Yes. There I am. Yes. One of the confusing things is, Mr. Lukic, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not cut out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's cut out. We see the line which -- with an arrow on the left picture, which goes in almost northerly direction, slightly to the west, if I could use that terminology, although it may have got nothing to do with north or west, but top of the picture and slightly to the left. That is indicated in the Mladic report as close to 170 degrees. Whereas, in the old sketch - that's the sketch to the right on our screen - it indicates 175 degrees. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you changed not the line but you changed the number related to that line from 175 into 170.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I changed the line very slightly to line it up with the centre of the crater in the new picture, which is more in line with 170. Also in the new picture, I have changed the line of -- with the line of 220 degrees may appear. You'll notice that that is completely different on both pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you help me, why did you change that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because when I'm now using the accurate bearings to the road, where 220 will appear will, of course, now move from using the old direction where it was on 275 now to a bearing of 260, it is moved to the right, and you'll notice it has moved quite significantly to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To make it clear, the lines, 275 and 175, or in your newest report, 170, are plotted on the basis of the features we see on the picture; whereas, the other line, the 220 degrees, is plotted on the basis of a compass measurement still taking the centre of the crater as its pivotal point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now we can see how things are moved in a photo, and we can also see in the report that was updated for our case where it says -- you can see in the Karadzic case that upper line, 275 degrees, in our case is -- it is now 260 degrees. There's a difference of 15 degrees in that, isn't there? And we can see that it did have an impact when you determined 220 degrees. How come that you changed the calculation by only 5 degrees? And we're talking about the centre of the crater. You changed the right parameter by 15 and the middle by only 5. How is that possible? I do not understand. Could you please explain? Because there are no changes in the sketch. The only changes that actually happened, happened to the calculation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we discussed yesterday, the -- the picture, the old picture, the one to the right here, was based upon not this particular part of the road. So the bearings don't relate directly to the picture as we -- as we discussed. So that is why I then amended the picture for this case to use the real bearings aligned to this picture and the curb. So the bearings on the original picture of 275 and 175 don't bear any direct connection to the picture on the left, because I have used new bearings. I have slightly altered the line through the centre of the crater to line it up as best as possible to the line of fire, and, of course, changed the -- the compass bearing to 220 to align to the new picture. So there is no direct relationship between the old picture and the new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, the picture in the newest report which gives the approximately 260 degree shows a line with an arrow pointing to left and to right. What you're telling us, if I understand you well, is that the approximately 260 degrees is not what that line depicts but it's the direction of the street you've taken from a map and not from this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in order to have accurate calculations, wouldn't you agree that if you want to make any calculations or make any measurements, you don't need the general direction of the street. You need what you see; that is, the exact direction of the curb zones -- of the curb on this part of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, why do you plot on such a photograph which is meant to prepare for calculations something we do not see in this photograph but, rather, something you took from a map which, as far as direction is concerned, does not necessarily reflect the direction of the curb stone in this specific part of that street? That's confusing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the -- the original photograph, I would agree, Your Honour. You are correct. As I used a -- as we know, a different part of the street, which does cause confusion. And that was a mistake on my behalf -- on my part for doing that, which is why I wanted to correct that in the picture for here. But I am -- a key point is I am not carrying out here a direct crater analysis. I'm using approximate bearings to just determine whether or not the crater is aligned to an approximately 170 or whether it is aligned to the 220/240. So I am not trying to determine the exact direction of the crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The way in which you present it is confusing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. Let's also keep in mind that if there's a difference of 10 degrees, the witness has explained what it's based on, that the difference between either 160, 170, or even 180, to 220 to 240 requires an additional 40, 50, or 60 degrees. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you made a mistake here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the original picture, I used -- yes, the way in which the numbers are displayed on this picture would be a mistake to show them in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's ignore 220 degrees. Let's focus on the blue line in the double photo and the line that goes through the centre of the crater. Between the original sketch and the updated sketch, or the new sketch, what is the biggest difference? Can you tell us what has been changed in the way the sketch was made? And let me tell you before you answer: Nothing has been changed. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do look very similar because I was trying to get a line as near as possible through the centre of the crater. So, yes, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only thing that has changed is the calculation. The right line by 15 degrees less, that's the blue line, and the middle line, which goes through the centre of the explosion and which should determine the direction of fire, has been changed by no more than 5 degrees. Would that be correct? And that's where I'm going to leave it off.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the -- the new picture, as I -- I notate in the report, I put down as a close to 170. I did not actually say that is actually 170.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what we are trying to -- we have been trying to say, because this should have read 155 or 160 degrees. 275 minus 15 is 260, and 175 minus 15 is 160; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep, that is correct. That is why I put down in the report it is close to 170. Because with the accuracy of the photograph then to be more accurate than that would be really impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to explain and perhaps to mark on the double photograph, but perhaps we should have it admitted into evidence first, Mr. Lukic, since that's what you seek.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number of the double photograph comparing the -- comparing the picture in the Karadzic report to the right with the picture in the Mladic report to the left would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D398 is admitted into evidence. Could the witness be provided with a marker so that he can explain exactly how he changed the upgoing arrowed line in the left picture, red, to go more precisely through the centre of the crater compared to the right one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the changes are minimal, Your Honour, because I have used -- it's approximately this -- the same line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you say it explains the difference of 10 degrees, as Mr. Lukic put to you, because if it is the same line, then if the blue, more or less, horizontal line moves from 275 degrees and if that other line doesn't really change - you say it's approximately the same line - then I would share Mr. -- I would be inclined to share Mr. Lukic's view that the 175 should go down to 160.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That -- that could be the case, Your Honour, yes. The -- it could be closer to 160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why did you then put it close to 170?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just, again, trying to make the point that not on accurate crater examination exactly where this is pointing but just making the point that this crater is facing closer to 170 than again to the 220.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's nothing you have to demonstrate. You have to provide us measurement, calculations, as precise as possible. That's what we expect an expert to do and not to say, Well, rather, if I could say, discretionary change the direction of one by 15 degrees and the other one just by 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. So we don't need any marking because the witness now says it's the same line. I don't know whether that is accurate, but let's leave it to that. It's at least approximately the same line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going ask you something else. Could people hear any noise when the shell was launched, and at what distance? In your report, you say that the observers -- and, if you will, this is in English, page 15, spilling over to page 16. You say that the UN observers could hear the sound of the shell which was launched at at distance of 1600 metres, and that if the shell had been launched at a distance of 2400 metres, it could not have been heard due to the configuration of the terrain, i.e., due to the hills and valleys. Can you see that in your report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this particular case, no sound was heard. So I make the point there on the report that when trying to ascertain a probable range, that if it was fired at 1600 where the observer was located, he should have heard it; where at the longer ranges, because of the configuration of the land, then he may not have heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you inspect the area? Did you ever go to Trebevic mountain?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to the mountain area there to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, do you understand the difference between they would not have heard it and they may not have heard it? Because the first is the language you use in the report. The second is the language you use now in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the lay of the land, the observer had a range of approximately 1600 direct line of sight. So in that case, they should have heard a sound. But the distances further to the rear, because of the mountains and the hills and so on, probably they -- hearing the sound would have been far more difficult. That's why I say they may not have heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although the report says "they would not have heard it," which is a far more definitive conclusion than "they may not have heard it."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you withdraw that conclusion that they would not have heard it and change it in they may not have heard it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that it's probably more realistic, Your Honour, to change to they may not have heard it in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More realistic, based on what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How sound travels around hill-sides, mountains, and so on. It depends on many, many, factors and difficult to be a definite one or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you refer us to either any studies on how sound travels in a mountainous area, at what distances, at what -- how strong the sound is? Do you have any sources or references or reports for that, or is it just an overall impression you've gained during your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's based on my experience in firing in these sort of conditions over the years, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that was when you were working in England?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was working in different countries around the world supporting different armies. It's never a cut-and-dried case whether or not you may hear it or you may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you tell us is: The more mountainous it is and the further the distance, it may be more difficult to hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we could take the usual -- we have the short sessions mainly -- and the short breaks as well mainly because that's the preference of Mr. Mladic. But if it would be your preference as well, we will follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know that the observation post, OP-1, UN observation post was very close to Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got that information here on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us take a look at 1D13912.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Lukic -- Have you studied the locations of observation posts in some detail closest to where the fire may have some from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was over there, yes, Your Honour, I travelled around that area in the vehicles and visited both sites, roughly the area where OP-1 was and then the areas up to the hills where some of the locations were as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And where OP-1 was, how did you find out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken there by -- the ICTY investigators took me to that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had prepared a map but I'm not sure whether the number is correct. 65 ter 23086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That doesn't look very much like a map, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we should have taken the early break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to continue, or what do you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd rather take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break under the present circumstances. The comedy of errors turns out to be a tragedy of errors. That's -- We take a break and resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Weber, Mr. Weber, at the cost of two or three euros, you'll buy such a thing, and whatever angle is there, on whatever map, you can immediately verify whether it's accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, did you have an opportunity to verify whether 2850 mills comes closer to 170 or 160?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's closer to 160, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. In my calculation, it's 160.3125. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have checked the number for our next document. I didn't have it previously because it was not uploaded but we managed to do that during the break, and I would like to inform both the Chamber and the Prosecution that this document hadn't been on the list, since this is a map into which we plotted some confidential information. We shall try, with Mr. Higgs, whether he is able to comment on it or not. Therefore, can I please have 1D1420.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you say "confidential information," can it be broadcast or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not confidential. It's some information from the report of this witness and some other information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there's no need to -- not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's just a map. Actually, it's a Google photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Higgs, we took an image from the Google Earth and we plotted 170/160 degrees bearings. We have also plotted 2400 metres distances, which corresponds to the distance that you have indicated as the VRS position where the fire originated. We also plotted the location of Colina Kapa and Bistrik Kula. Colina Kapa is the position at which OP-1 observation post was situated. Would this correspond to what you know? Because you said you have toured the area, is it this true reflection of the ground that you have visited?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These two red lines converge and meet at the point where the Markale market is. Can you confirm that? Or if you cannot see it, we are fine with that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- seems to be in the approximate location from what I can see on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you said that the first position of the Serbian forces would be at 2400 metres, did you visit that specific area, and did you notice whether there was any access road to that location, and also whether there was a convenient place to put a mortar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We drove generally round that -- that hilled area where you have 2400-metre symbols. We looked at some of the roads, and -- and some areas where there could possibly be mortar locations, but we didn't do an extensive survey of the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Mr. Hogan's work who made some very detailed visits to the area and who checked where the possible locations could be? He was, just to mention it by the way, an ICTY investigator and a witness.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen any report or paperwork concerning that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this image from the Google Earth into evidence because we are going to need it in future, in order to show some other Google images.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I asked that remain marked for identification so I can check the information. Also if Mr. Lukic could provide me with whatever the confidential information that is the -- is the basis of this over the next break so I could further check that at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to borrow it, just tell me, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's okay. There is no -- any confidential information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That must be then some kind of confusion because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no confidential information entered on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1420 receives number D399, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please now have 1D1392.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, by a simple click on Google Earth one can get a cross-section of the ground, and this is what our expert did in -- indeed. In the upper part, you see the image. You see the market-place at 170 degrees angle to 2400 metres distance. We can see Colina Kapa and Bistrik Kula as well in the lower part is the cross-section of the ground from the position at 2400 metres towards the Markale market-place. Since, as say you, visited this area, would you agree that between these two locations, there is no obstacle whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just confirm. The cross-section, is that from the market-place to the position of 2400, or is it a cross-section looking across this picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] What do you mean by cross-section? Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You used the word, Mr. Lukic, first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So is this cross-section of how the picture at the bottom, the cross-section of how the land rises, is this taken from the market-place up to where the possible firing position could take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Possible firing position. I do understand 170 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 170 degrees [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 170 degrees --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- over a distance of 2400 metres and that is [Overlapping speakers] ... projected 2400 metres, I take it, not because you know that the distance projected is shorter, if you go upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's projected from 2400 up to Markale market-place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Lukic, if I measure a distance, if I do it on a map, then, on the map, it shows to be shorter that in reality it may be because it also has to cover an inclination, also has to cover a difference in altitude. Now is the 24 [sic] metres, the real distance or is it the projected distance on a map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's projected distance on the map, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Higgs, since you have been to the area, does this correspond to what you saw, that is to say, that between the location at 2400 metres distance to the Markale market, there are no natural obstacles that would prevent the spread of the sound?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no hills in the way, as such, just the -- the vegetation, the tall trees, on that particular slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we tender this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would object at the time. We ask that it remain marked for identification until the expert comes and testifies. The Prosecution will also express its concern about using angled views on Google Earth to actually depict, in fact, elevations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification. It was just to illustrate, Mr. Lukic, that you took this angled projection because you can't make measurements in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think measurements would be included as well, so probably our expert would testify on that issue as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But that is certainly unclear at this moment. Angles, et cetera, of course, change if you change the projection from anything else than 90 degrees rectangular. It will be marked for identification. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1392 receives number D400, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you said that a distance was 2400 metres, did you measure it by walking down the road, or did you take your measurement on the map? What was the basis for this assertion of yours?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance was taken off the flat distance off the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, you made your measurement from the map without taking the elevation of the ground into consideration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The measurement was done directly off -- off the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D1393, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we look at that, Mr. Lukic, could I ask you to carefully also verify the markings on the map you showed us a minute ago, indicating lines for 160 and 170 degrees, because it seems that there's more than 10 degrees of difference there. Could you please check that very carefully. It seems that the plotting is not accurate. To me, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have that gadget in my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can buy it for two or three euros in every shop where -- it's not that difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that both Mr. Weber and I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You haven't listened carefully enough at secondary school, I'm afraid. Please proceed. But I'm quite willing to borrow it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I will check that as well but I have to work with what I have in my hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the next one we need is 1D1393.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same procedure is applied here. Only now by using a Google Earth photograph, I applied -- or we applied a 160-degrees angle. Do you know whether this is also consistent with what you saw on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the area is -- is -- we're still looking at the same area. I obviously cannot verify or deny your line you have for 160 degrees there. Just seemed to be a picture of the same area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this one to be marked for identification as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1393 receives number D401, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, you marked this distance as the distance from which a mortar shell could have been fired with charge 3 - is that correct? - and I'm talking about the distance of 2400 metres.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness, have you taken into consideration the difference in elevation when you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- calculated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Because, although we have a distance of 2400 metres we draw on the map, when a mortar is elevated above the horizontal, it actually gives the mortar longer range. It's actually -- in the range tables there was a calculation where you can add and increase an altitude onto the distance that the mortar can actually achieve. So I took that into account when looking at the areas around this -- on the map of this area around 2400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just -- so it was considered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, you relied on Mr. Eric Bleakely's statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In regard to which parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In regard of the market-place incident of the 28th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the statements I looked at, but obviously not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to avoid some misquotation, I would prefer for us to look at 1D1394. Let us look at 1D1394.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the statement that you had relied upon. In the English is Mr. Bleakely's statement, and we need page 11; and in the B/C/S, we need page 13. Here, Mr. Bleakely says that the HALO system was in use on the ground which is the Royal Artillery system, which involves the disposition of sound sensors for artillery and mortar fire. This system would have registered in Sarajevo all firing from the city. Excessive noise would hamper the sensors who are unable to deal with excessive noise, and it is also said that HALO cannot make a distinction between the detonation of a round against a firing. Is it true that this particular system -- are you aware that on that particular day, this system did not register any firing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I have to base that on would be this report. And I believe in this report they did not pick up anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so we have some precise information, I read that -- that the statement here says that it would have picked up anything that had been fired from inside the city. And I just warranted to make that clear just because it wasn't incorporated in the previous -- so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, are you familiar with this system? And is it possible that with its beam it can pick up only the sound coming from one direction, or should it pick up the sounds coming from all directions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the system, but I'm not a technical expert on this piece of equipment, so I'm afraid I couldn't give you a -- an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I saw you nodding yes where the transcript -- after my question whether you agreed or not has no answer in the transcript. But you apparently agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the gentleman cannot tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I mean the previous one, reading the statement. Mr. Weber said something about it. I asked you whether you agreed.

utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's difference in the translation, Your Honour. I was reading from B/C/S. And it says: From the city. And the fact is that, in English, it is: Inside the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Higgs, let me ask you something about the traces on the tarmac and the position of the stabiliser following an explosion of a mortar shell. According to you, what kind of charge is required for a 120-millimetre shells for the stabiliser to become embedded into the pavement? And I'm talking about the pavement of the same texture as the one in front of the Markale market-place, so to be either embedded or to remain at the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue of whether a tail-fin will embed in the ground is dependant on many factors. And the hardness of the ground, of course, is one of those factors. And it's also dependant the velocity the round is travelling. Normally, the higher the velocity on the higher charges, and by that I mean charges 5 and 6, would normally have a higher probability that the tail-fins will still be lodged in the crater. But this is not always the case. It's just a higher probability that that will be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Charge 4, according to you, would not necessarily be embedded in the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I assume that the same applies to a charge 3, in your view; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, could I ask you, if you say charge 4 would not necessarily be embedded in the asphalt. You earlier said that there are many factors to be considered. What speed at impact did you have in mind when you're talking about charge 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not got the velocity in front of me, but normally for the charges 3s and 4s, the -- the middle charge of velocities that can be fired, for their tail-fins to be in the ground we normally expect that to be in very soft ground, and, again, the probability of happening is quite low. The probability goes up when you fire the higher charges, i.e., charges 5 and 6, because they have fire -- greater muzzle velocities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is a rather general statement. The higher the velocity, muzzle velocity, and therefore the higher velocity at impact would enhance the chance that the tail-fin would embed in the grounds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you something about radar Cymbeline. You have perused the comprehensive UNPROFOR report that was done at the request of the UN, about the same event. Let's look at 65 ter 30280. Perhaps it is already part of the evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is document MFI'd as P2605, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. [Interpretation] In this report, we would like to look at page 11 in English and page 17 in B/C/S. This is just to show that -- or, rather, what materials were used, what sources were used, for the purpose of this report. And now we would like to see bullet point 4 in this report. Unfortunately, I do not have the page number for -- for this paragraph. In English, I would like to look at page 3, and the same page in -- in the B/C/S version, please. The page numbers do not tally, although this is how I recorded them in preparing my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next page in -- next page in B/C/S, therefore. Yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, this is not what I need. There must have been some error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said you wanted to look at paragraph -- at item 4, or bullet point 4, which is fuses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the fuses are there now in B/C/S, unless you wanted to address any other part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the top of the page? Maybe I can calculate, since I have ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the subject you want to address?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to talk about Cymbeline --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cymbeline.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- radar. And I want to read one portion from this report, but ... I will continue without the document, since I cannot locate. Give me one second. I have one document.
